name: zero-added-key-enlarges-the-denominator
why: A key added at 0.0 costs nothing in the numerator and its full weight in the denominator, so the denominator counts penalties that were added and never a fixed weight table. Dropping the media key from max gives 3.5/4 = 0.875; summing all twenty shipped weights gives 3.5/35.5.

name: one-key-many-penalties
why: AddNumber appends one penalty per unit of difference, so a single key can enlarge the denominator by its weight several times over. Three medium penalties at weight 1.0 plus one album penalty at weight 3.0 is a denominator of 6, not of 4.

name: only-key-carries-weight-zero
why: The added-key view keeps a key whose weight is 0.0 and the nonzero view drops it, which is the pair of views port hazard 4 is about. The same fixture makes the denominator zero, so the aggregate must return 0.0 where an unguarded division returns NaN.

name: no-penalties-at-all
why: The other reachable zero denominator: an accumulator nothing was added to scores 0.0 rather than NaN.

name: nonzero-view-sorts-by-descending-distance
why: The two keys are added in ascending order of weighted distance, so an unsorted view or one keyed on (distance, key) puts year first. The added-key and generic views keep insertion order and are the control.

name: equal-distances-break-on-key-ascending
why: Both keys weigh 1.0 and carry the same penalty, so only the second sort key can order them, and it orders ascending while the distance orders descending.
